fetchedNote: Sourced 2026-10-18, bank-published figures only — no broker/remittance-fintech sites. 'official' = the bank states this number directly. 'computed' = derived by comparing the bank's own dated forex-card-rate PDF against the interbank rate on that SAME date (frankfurter.dev), not written as a bps figure anywhere by the bank itself. 'partial' = bank-published but narrow in scope. 'unavailable' = genuinely not found, not estimated.

senderBanks.name: Deutsche Bank
senderBanks.feeBreakdown: €10.00 minimum (data-transmission transfer) + 0.15% commission (‰ 1.5) + €1.55 SWIFT message fee, SHA case
senderBanks.ourSurchargeBreakdown: Fremdspesenpauschale (OUR) — flat third-party-expenses fee Deutsche Bank itself charges when the sender selects OUR
senderBanks.note: Deutsche Bank's own official price list (business/corporate accounts, German-language PDF dated March 2026). Private/retail terms may differ — not independently confirmed from a Deutsche Bank retail source. No daily rate sheet applies here: this is a transfer fee schedule, not a currency conversion rate.

senderBanks.name: Sparkasse
senderBanks.feeBreakdown: €30 minimum currency-conversion commission (0.025%, min €30) — one regional branch's own published figure, not national
senderBanks.note: “Sparkasse” is not one bank — roughly 350 independently operated regional savings banks, each with its own price list. This is Sparkasse Rastatt-Gernsbach's own published figure (effective 2023-01-01), used as the only concrete bank-published example found, not a national fee.

receiverBanks.name: ICICI Bank
receiverBanks.fxDetail: ICICI's own live forex-card-rate page: EUR TT Buying ₹104.50 (as displayed 2026-10-16). Interbank EUR/INR that same date (frankfurter.dev): 106.864. Spread = (106.864−104.50)/106.864 ≈ 221bps.
receiverBanks.note: FX markup is computed, not bank-stated as a bps figure — see fxDetail. No inward handling fee was shown on this page, so that field stays unavailable.

receiverBanks.name: SBI
receiverBanks.feeBreakdown: ₹50 + 18% GST — SBI's own published retail cross-border remittance charges
receiverBanks.note: SBI's own forex card rate PDF (dated 17-10-2026, EUR TT Buy ₹105.30) is explicit that these card rates apply only to transactions between ₹10 lakh and ₹20 lakh — ‘for transactions of value less than Rs. 10 lakhs, please contact the nearest branch.’ Our €1000 (~₹1 lakh) scenario is below that floor, so SBI's own document says this rate doesn't apply here; the markup stays unavailable rather than borrowed from the wrong bracket.

receiverBanks.name: HDFC Bank
receiverBanks.fxDetail: HDFC's own Treasury Forex Card Rates PDF: EUR T.T. Buying (Inw Rem) ₹104.38 (sheet dated 16/10/2026 12:22 PM). Interbank EUR/INR that same date (frankfurter.dev): 106.864. Spread = (106.864−104.38)/106.864 ≈ 233bps. The PDF itself states these card rates apply to retail transactions up to ₹20 lakh equivalent — our €1000 scenario qualifies.
receiverBanks.note: Inward fee ₹0 and the TT Buying rate are both HDFC's own published figures; the bps spread is computed from them (see fxDetail), not stated by HDFC as a markup percentage.

receiverBanks.name: IDFC First Bank
